item.title: Totó La Momposina, Colombian Artist Who Elevated Caribbean Folk Music to Global Stage, Dead at 85
item.description:
[Ethereal music plays in the background]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we celebrate the lives and legacies of legendary artists. Today, we're remembering a true icon of Caribbean folk music, Totó La Momposina, who passed away on May 17th at the age of 85.
[Soft music transition]
Host: Born in 1940 in Talaigua Nuevo, Colombia, Totó La Momposina came from a musical family and began performing in the 1960s. She went on to study music and folklore in Bogotá, Paris, and Cuba, laying the foundation for her global breakthrough.
[Short music clip of Totó La Momposina's music plays]
Host: That breakthrough came in the 1990s with her album "La Candela Viva", released through Peter Gabriel's Real World Records. This introduction to Colombian folk music helped elevate her to the global stage.
[Music transitions back to the host]
Host: Totó La Momposina's achievements include a feature on Calle 13's "Latinoamérica", which reached number 9 on the Latin Digital Song Sales chart in 2011. Her legacy extends far beyond her chart success, however.
[Respectful pause]
Host: The Colombian president, Gustavo Petro, and the Ministry of Culture have paid tribute to Totó La Momposina, honoring her dedication to preserving and promoting traditional Caribbean music. Her family has also shared a heartfelt message, describing her as a woman who carried the culture and memory of the Colombian people to the world.
[Soft music continues to play]
Host: Totó La Momposina's body will be transported from Mexico to Colombia on May 27th, where a posthumous tribute will be held to celebrate her life and work. We join her family, friends, and fans in mourning the loss of this incredible artist, and we celebrate her enduring legacy in the world of music.
[Closing music plays]
Host: Thank you for listening. Totó La Momposina may be gone, but her music and spirit will continue to inspire and uplift us for generations to come.
